title: Commercial passenger vehicle reform legalising ride-share (Victoria)
summary: Victoria announced in August 2016 it would legalise ride-share with a transition package; the Commercial Passenger Vehicle Industry Act 2017 passed on 10 August 2017 (first version in force 23 August 2017) and the full new framework, including abolition of taxi licences in favour of registration, operated from 2 July 2018.

instruments.title: Commercial Passenger Vehicle Industry Amendment (Further Reforms) Act 2017

commenced.what: First version of the 2017 Act in force (initial provisions)
Act came into full operation (new registration and accreditation framework)

direction_rationale: Legalising app-based ride-share removes the legal barrier to entry created by taxi/hire-car licence quotas, adding a new type of supplier and price competition in point-to-point transport.
comparison: States that had not yet legalised ride-sharing (ACT Oct 2015 first, NT Dec 2017/Feb 2018 last)
confounders: taxi licence compensation and per-trip levies
ABN registration by gig drivers inflates business counts

verified.notes: Announcement date is from an AAP/SBS report (secondary); which provisions commenced on 23 Aug 2017 (and whether ride-share was lawful from then) was not confirmed from the Act's endnotes.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use. Primary commencement chosen on 15 October 2026 as the date the change described in the title took effect; confirm on review.

assessment.summary: Legalised app-based ride-share alongside taxis, removing the barrier that capped taxi and hire-car licences placed on point-to-point transport. Nationally, businesses in taxi and other road transport rose from about 16,000 in June 2015 to about 39,500 in June 2019 as drivers joined (ABS business counts).

marks.reason: Removes the legal barrier that taxi and hire-car licence caps placed on booked point-to-point trips.
Legalises app-based booking and pricing across the industry.
A modest distortion: a per-trip levy funded the transition package.

assessment.confidence_note: The archived econometric evaluation could not identify the effect on business entry, because ride-share drivers are counted with taxis and the data changed at the same time.
